Be Part of the PCBWay 7th Project Design Contest! by: PCBWay Sep 03,2024 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News We are glad to announce that PCBWay 7th Project Design Contest has arrived. Prior to this, PCBWay successfully held six design contests. In each contest, we saw many eye-catching projects shared by outstanding and creative electronic engineers and enthusiasts. PCBWay 7th Project Design Contest will continue the previous purpose, which is to encourage more and more people to explore the charm of electronic design and participate in it. PCBWay 7th Project Design Contest: https://www.pcbway.com/activity/7th-project-design-contest.html . In this contest, in addition to the two themes of Electronic Project and Mechanical Project that have appeared before, we also introduced STM32 Project, hoping to give designers more room to perform. The contest will start on September 2nd, 2024, and project submissions will be accepted until January 19th, 2025. After this, the judging phase will begin, and the final winners will be announced on the PCBWay Blog on March 10th, 2025. Two ways to participate in the contest: Go to the contest page, find the Participate Now button and click it. In this case, the submitted project will automatically be entered into the competition; participants only need to select the theme of entry. Please note that if you are submitting a mechanical project, please switch to the CNC |3D Printing Project page. After filling in all the project information, simply click "Submit" at the bottom of the page. Go to the SharedProject Community ( https://www.pcbway.com/project/shareproject/ ) and click Create a project. Select the theme you are going to participate in. Similarly, if you are submitting a mechanical project, please switch to the CNC |3D Printing Project page. Hint: Sharing complete project files, including Gerber, BOM, Centroid file, schematics, 3D files, and so on will increase the chances of receiving a higher score. China will (i) modify accordingly the application of the additional ad valorem rate of duty on articles of the United States set forth in Announcement of the Customs Tariff Commission of the State Council No. 4 of 2025, by suspending 24 percentage points of that rate for an initial period of 90 days, while retaining the remaining additional ad valorem rate of 10 percent on those articles, and removing the modified additional ad valorem rates of duty on those articles imposed by Announcement of the Customs Tariff Commission of the State Council No. 5 of 2025 and Announcement of the Customs Tariff Commission of the State Council No. 6 of 2025; and (ii) adopt all necessary administrative measures to suspend or remove the non-tariff countermeasures taken against the United States since April 2, 2025. After taking the aforementioned actions, the Parties will establish a mechanism to continue discussions about economic and trade relations. As required, the two sides may conduct working-level consultations on relevant economic and trade issues. https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefings-statements/2025/05/joint-statement-on-u-s-china-economic-and-trade-meeting-in-geneva/ Updated on April 25th **Presidential Executive Order on Tariff Adjustments for Chinese Goods** On April 8, 2025 (local time), U.S. President Donald Trump issued an executive order announcing the following tariff measures on goods originating from China (including Hong Kong, China): 1. **Elimination of De Minimis Exemption for Chinese-origin Goods** 2. **Additional 125%+20% (If it is the category under 9903.01.32 or 9903.01.33, the tariff exemption is 125%) Tariff on High-value Chinese Goods** 3.Fedex Official: For B2C shipments, a valid FedEx account number is required. 4.If the product falls under HTS categories 9903.01.32 or 9903.01.33, it qualifies for a 125% tariff exemption. However, DHL’s customs declaration system may inaccurately apply or fail to recognize the 125% exemption. If the recipient finds that the product is indeed eligible for the exemption but the 125% duty relief was not applied, they must file a dispute with DHL immediately, as there is a strict deadline for appeals. By the time the sender notices the issue, the appeal window may have already closed. Note: Regarding why your social security number/tax ID number/IRS number/importer number is needed when shipping, please check out this official article for explanation: Why is an overseas supplier asking for my social security number/tax ID number/IRS number/importer number? ============================================================================================== by the way： Importers - Why is an overseas supplier asking for my social security number/tax ID number/IRS number/importer number? When an individual or company purchases goods from an overseas supplier, U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) considers them the ultimate importer. The ultimate importer can clear the goods or have a Customs Broker clear them on their behalf. If the supplier hires a carrier that provides door to door service, the carrier service usually has brokers in their supply chain to clear the goods on behalf of the ultimate importer. If a formal entry is required, CBP regulations require the broker to put the ultimate importer's identification number on the CBP Form 7501- Entry Summary. The ultimate importer's identification number is either the Employers Identification Number (EIN) tax identification number assigned by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) or the importer's social security number. The EIN is issued for the purpose of tax administration and are not intended for participation in any other activities (e.g., tax lien auction or sales, lotteries). For additional information about EIN, please visit the IRS web page "Apply for an Employer Identification (EIN) Online." Goods are usually cleared informally when they are for personal use, under $2500 in value, and are not in commercial quantities. A formal entry is usually required for commercial importations valued over $2,500. Because many foreign merchants are aware that CBP requires an identification number for the ultimate importer for formal entries, they will often request the purchaser's social security number to include on export documents that the broker will subsequently rely on to prepare the CBP entry. It should be noted that paperwork for goods sent by courier service does ask for an importer number, whether the import qualifies for an informal entry or not. Courier services file CBP entries electronically, and the software system they use requires an identification number to be provided for the recipient of the goods. If an identification number is not provided, the courier service is required to file a paper entry, which is extremely time-consuming and in the world of "Overnight Delivery" not practical. The end result is that most courier services will not accept packages for international delivery to U.S. residents if a recipient's identification number is not provided by the shipper. Goods sent through the international postal service that are under $2500 in value generally do not require an importer number to be cleared through CBP. It’s Trickier Than You Think. But because of an ever-changing patchwork of trade rules, not every product will be charged an astronomical tariff, trade lawyers, customs brokers and importers say. In some cases, tariffs will pile on other tariffs. In other instances, they can reduce costs, while other times they can cancel out new ones. The new 125 percent rate that President Trump imposed will in many cases be added on top of long-existing duties. There are four main categories of tariffs that are imposed on goods from China. Note: The tariff on auto parts comes into effect in early May. The average provided for the base rate is calculated by the World Trade Organization, which computes an average of all tariff lines. A large share of U.S. imports are assigned a 0% duty, but there are some very high rates in the tariff schedule. Rates ultimately depend on what is imported, what materials are used (from where), which special rates are applied and what sorts of products are exempt. Note: Regarding why your social security number/tax ID number/IRS number/importer number is needed when shipping, please check out this official article for explanation: Why is an overseas supplier asking for my social security number/tax ID number/IRS number/importer number? ============================================================================================== by the way： Importers - Why is an overseas supplier asking for my social security number/tax ID number/IRS number/importer number? When an individual or company purchases goods from an overseas supplier, U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) considers them the ultimate importer. The ultimate importer can clear the goods or have a Customs Broker clear them on their behalf. If the supplier hires a carrier that provides door to door service, the carrier service usually has brokers in their supply chain to clear the goods on behalf of the ultimate importer. If a formal entry is required, CBP regulations require the broker to put the ultimate importer's identification number on the CBP Form 7501- Entry Summary. The ultimate importer's identification number is either the Employers Identification Number (EIN) tax identification number assigned by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) or the importer's social security number. The EIN is issued for the purpose of tax administration and are not intended for participation in any other activities (e.g., tax lien auction or sales, lotteries). For additional information about EIN, please visit the IRS web page "Apply for an Employer Identification (EIN) Online." Goods are usually cleared informally when they are for personal use, under $2500 in value, and are not in commercial quantities. A formal entry is usually required for commercial importations valued over $2,500. Because many foreign merchants are aware that CBP requires an identification number for the ultimate importer for formal entries, they will often request the purchaser's social security number to include on export documents that the broker will subsequently rely on to prepare the CBP entry. It should be noted that paperwork for goods sent by courier service does ask for an importer number, whether the import qualifies for an informal entry or not. Courier services file CBP entries electronically, and the software system they use requires an identification number to be provided for the recipient of the goods. If an identification number is not provided, the courier service is required to file a paper entry, which is extremely time-consuming and in the world of "Overnight Delivery" not practical. The end result is that most courier services will not accept packages for international delivery to U.S. residents if a recipient's identification number is not provided by the shipper. Goods sent through the international postal service that are under $2500 in value generally do not require an importer number to be cleared through CBP. Meet PCBWay at electronica 2024! by: PCBWay Oct 18,2024 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News Once again, we welcome the famous technology event electronica in Munich, Germany! Since the first exhibition was held in 1964, electronica has gradually grown and now covers the entire world of electronics, including the micro- and nano-worlds of semiconductor and micro systems technology, as well as measurement and sensor technology, display technology and vehicle electronics, etc., which is the best choice for any technology enthusiasts and industry practitioners. PCBWay has participated in theelectronica many times and has received a warm response every time. At the exhibition, everyone has the opportunity to get close to our various products and fully evaluate the performance and quality of our products, which is far beyond the scope of online communication. Verify Now Blog > PCBWay Fabrication Toolkit for Kicad PCBWay Fabrication Toolkit for Kicad by: PCBWay Oct 11,2023 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News Recently, PCBWay added a plug-in called PCBWay Fabrication Toolkit to Kicad: With just one click of the mouse, four files can be exported from the layout file automatically: Gerber file, IPC-Netlist file, BOM file and Pick and Place file, which can significantly improves the efficiency of pre-production work. Installation from the Official KiCad Repositories After installation, the plugin will appear on the right side of the navigation bar. And users can use it to export all the production files with just a click. Process demonstration： Sending the files to PCBWay, and they can be used for production after being reviewed by the staff. Note: If you want to place an assembly order, please be sure to add MPN information to the BOM. This can help the quoter source the devices you need more accurately. Manual installation Except for the way mentioned before, you can also download the latest ZIP file from https://github.com/pcbway/PCBWay-Fabrication-Toolkit-for-KiCad: Open the "Plugin and Content Manager" from the main window of KiCad and install the ZIP file via "Install from File". About BOM Through BOM files, we can get all information of the components used in your design. In order to speed up the quotation process, we need this information: 1. Designator (necessary) 2. Quantity (necessary) 3. MPN/Part Number (necessary) 4. Package/Footprint (necessary) 5. Manufacturer (optional) 6. Description/value (optional) If you have more suggestions, please leave a message below, PCBWay has committed to providing everyone with high-quality services. Verify Now Blog > PCBWay and Tindie Launch the 2026 AI Hardware Design Contest PCBWay and Tindie Launch the 2026 AI Hardware Design Contest by: Mila Oct 30,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News design contest ai contest pcbway contest PCBWay is teaming up with Tindie to launch the 2026 AI Hardware Design Contest , inviting makers, engineers, developers, students, and hardware enthusiasts worldwide to explore the possibilities of combining artificial intelligence with hardware innovation. Whether you're building an AI-powered smart device, developing an intelligent embedded system, or experimenting with a creative DIY project, this is your opportunity to turn an idea into a working prototype<dynamic-value> your creation with the global maker community, and compete for a share of the $2,500 prize pool. Registration and project submissions open on November 1, 2026 (PT). Get your ideas ready and join the challenge! About the PCBWay × Tindie AI Hardware Design Contest Artificial intelligence is creating new possibilities for hardware development. From intelligent sensors and smart home devices to robotics and edge AI applications, AI is changing how electronic devices interact with people and the world around them. The PCBWay × Tindie AI Hardware Design Contest aims to encourage makers and developers to explore these possibilities through practical hardware projects. By combining PCBWay's PCB manufacturing and engineering capabilities with Tindie's hardware maker community, we hope to support innovative ideas and help more creators turn their concepts into real-world products. Whether you're an experienced hardware engineer or an independent maker exploring AI for the first time, you're welcome to participate. Unlock Color PCB Printing with PCBWay! by: PCBWay Mar 08,2024 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News Color PCB Printing PCBWay Service Nowadays, traditional PCB printing technology can no longer meet the aesthetic requirements of modern circuit board production. To better fulfill customers' design needs, we are pleased to announce that PCBWay has introduced UV printing equipment. This equipment utilizes UV-curable inks to achieve high-quality image printing on various materials, including fiberglass boards, metal substrates, ceramic substrates, flexible boards, and rigid-flex boards. Entrance https://www.pcbway.com/orderonline.aspx Prerequisites for Ordering Maximum size for a single piece: 270*470MM; Selection of background soldermask color required. Design Specifications Drill holes, traces, soldermasks, and outline designs must comply with specifications. Avoid placing colored characters in areas with solder mask openings, such as surface-mount pads or through-hole pads. What kind of files should be provided for color printing? Method One : Draw colored characters on the silkscreen layer of the Gerber and provide reference pictures. For example: Method Two : If you include information about colored silkscreen in the Gerber layer, each individual color must have its own layer. If there is only one layer, we can only print one color. [This method is not recommended] . If you need to print in multiple colors, we recommend using method One and providing us with a reference picture. 4.Please send the images you want to print on the PCB in the following formats: AI, PDF, JPEG, PNG, TIFF, etc., and indicate your desired printing location on the board. 5.If the image contains a QR code, please ensure that the QR code can be accurately scanned and recognized. Note : If you choose UV printing Multi-color, we will use matte UV color printing by default. When designing the colored characters on the bottom layer, be careful not to design the colored characters as mirrored inverses. (The process of color printing is different from that of standard PCB silkscreen printing. When printing colorful characters on the bottom layer, they are printed with the bottom layer of the PCB facing up.) For situations where the entire top or bottom side requires full-color printing, regardless of the solder mask color you choose, we will use a white solder mask on the full-color printed side and then proceed with the color printing. This is for a better printing effect. Please upload the print image, positioning image, and Gerber in one compressed file. By providing a clear positioning image and necessary instructions, you can assist PCBWay in accurately determining and achieving the desired printing position. Matte UV Color Printing vs. Glossy UV Color Printing Matte ink does not increase the overall thickness, and the PCB's appearance looks smooth. Glossy ink increases the overall thickness and may affect the soldering of component pads. The appearance is beautiful but uneven. Features Adopting UV-LED lamp curing, which enables instant drying, can significantly enhances production efficiency. UV printing technology employs UV-curable inks, ensuring firm and clear printing information resistant to fading, thus enhancing product identification and aesthetics. The normal print survives SMT reflow. Since it's ink, there will be some discoloration. UV printing technology can present images in various colors and styles, meeting customers' personalized requirements. Professional industrial-grade UV printers support high-precision printing, delivering exquisite results whether on flat panels or rolled materials. Unlike traditional printing methods, UV printing does not produce volatile organic compounds during the production process, ensuring air quality in the production workshop and providing employees with a safer and healthier working environment. FAQ on UV Printing: Can the UV printed surface be cleaned with water? Yes, it can be cleaned with water. Can the UV printed surface be cleaned with alcohol? It is more difficult to clean after being exposed to alcohol and baked (currently, the board undergoes a short baking process after UV printing). However, with increased contact time with alcohol and vigorous scrubbing, it can be removed. This also depends on whether the UV is on the copper surface or the solder mask surface. How hard is the UV printed surface (sensitivity to scratches)? The UV surface is not sensitive to scratches. However, compared to the solder mask, it is less scratch-resistant because UV printing is ink that is sprayed on and is relatively thin. Welcome to give it a try if you're interested! Besides, PCBWay will continue to enhance its manufacturing capabilities to bring more choices and personalized services to customers in the future. Verify Now Blog > How Does a Thermistor Circuit Work? NTC, PTC, and PCB Layout How Does a Thermistor Circuit Work? NTC, PTC, and PCB Layout by: Mila Nov 18,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCB Design & Layout thermistor circuit NTC thermistor PTC thermistor NTC vs PTC thermistor thermistor pcb Temperature monitoring is essential for protecting electronic components, maintaining system stability, and ensuring reliable operation. Whether preventing a battery from overheating or keeping an industrial motor within its operating temperature range, accurate temperature sensing plays an important role. Among various temperature sensors, thermistors are widely used because of their simple structure, low cost, and fast response. This article explains how thermistors work, explores common measurement circuits, discusses key performance parameters, and compares NTC and PTC thermistors to help guide component selection and PCB design . 1. What Is a Thermistor? Understanding How It Works Working Principle: A thermistor is a resistor whose resistance changes significantly with temperature. The name comes from the combination of "thermal" and "resistor." Its key characteristic is that its resistance varies in response to changes in its own temperature. This property allows a thermistor to convert temperature, a physical quantity, into a change in electrical resistance, which can then be converted into a measurable voltage signal through an external circuit. Figure 1. Different types of thermistors Two Main Types: Based on how their resistance changes with temperature, thermistors are generally divided into two categories: NTC (Negative Temperature Coefficient) Thermistors: Their resistance decreases as temperature increases. NTC thermistors are among the most widely used temperature-sensing components due to their low cost and high sensitivity. Common applications include battery temperature monitoring, power management, and household appliance temperature control. PTC (Positive Temperature Coefficient) Thermistors: Their resistance increases as temperature rises. Depending on their materials and resistance characteristics, PTC thermistors can be further divided into two types: Nonlinear (Switching-Type) PTC Thermistors: Their resistance increases sharply near a specific temperature, known as the Curie temperature. They are commonly used for overcurrent protection, overtemperature protection, and resettable fuses. Linear PTC Thermistors: Typically made from silicon, these devices have a relatively stable positive temperature coefficient. Their resistance increases approximately linearly with temperature, making them suitable for temperature measurement applications. Simply put, an NTC thermistor behaves like a component that offers less resistance as it gets hotter. A linear PTC thermistor works in the opposite way: its resistance increases with temperature, generally in a more uniform and predictable manner. 2. How to Read a Thermistor: Two Common Measurement Circuits A thermistor does not generate an electrical signal on its own. It requires an external excitation source to convert its resistance changes into a measurable voltage signal. The following are two commonly used measurement circuits. Voltage Divider Circuit (Constant-Voltage Excitation) Figure 2. Thermistor in a voltage divider configuration This is one of the simplest and most cost-effective thermistor measurement methods. A thermistor is connected in series with a fixed reference resistor and supplied by a stable voltage source, such as VCC. By measuring the voltage across one of the resistors, the temperature information can be obtained. Working Principle: When the temperature changes, the thermistor's resistance changes accordingly. According to the voltage divider principle, the output voltage, V_TEMP, also changes. By measuring this voltage, the thermistor resistance can be calculated, and the corresponding temperature can then be determined. Advantages: The circuit is simple, requires few components, and has a low implementation cost, making it suitable for many conventional temperature-sensing applications. Considerations: Variations in the supply voltage VCC can affect V_TEMP and introduce measurement errors. To reduce this effect, a ratiometric measurement method can be used. For example, the same voltage source can serve as both the excitation voltage for the divider and the ADC reference voltage. This helps cancel out the effects of supply voltage fluctuations. Constant-Current Excitation Circuit Figure 3. Thermistor measurement using constant-current excitation Another approach is to use a precision constant-current source (I BIAS ) to supply a stable current to the thermistor. Working Principle: According to Ohm's law, V = I × R. Since the current flowing through the thermistor remains constant, the voltage across it, V_TEMP, is proportional to its resistance: V TEMP = I BIAS × R THERMISTOR When the temperature changes and the thermistor resistance varies, the output voltage changes accordingly. Advantages: Within the operating range of the current source, the output voltage is linearly proportional to the thermistor resistance. This makes resistance measurement and signal processing more straightforward, especially in applications requiring relatively high measurement accuracy. Considerations: The accuracy, temperature drift, and output voltage range of the current source all affect measurement results. In addition, excessive excitation current can cause thermistor self-heating. Therefore, the bias current must be selected carefully. The Next Step: Signal Processing The resulting analog voltage signal, V TEMP , is typically sent to an analog-to-digital converter (ADC) input on a microcontroller (MCU) for digital processing. Alternatively, it can be sent to a voltage comparator and compared with a preset threshold voltage to implement a basic overtemperature alarm. Figure 4. Overtemperature threshold detection using a thermistor and comparator 3. Key Parameters for Improving Thermistor Performance and Accuracy When selecting a thermistor, its nominal resistance is not the only parameter to consider. The following characteristics also play an important role in determining temperature measurement accuracy, stability, and overall circuit complexity. Resistance Tolerance Resistance tolerance refers to the allowable deviation between a thermistor's actual resistance and its nominal resistance at a specified temperature, typically 25°C. For example, a tolerance of ±1% means the actual resistance can vary within 1% of the specified nominal value at that temperature. NTC Thermistors: The resistance tolerance of an NTC thermistor depends not only on its nominal resistance at 25°C but also on the tolerance of its B-value and other material characteristics. Therefore, even if an NTC thermistor has a resistance tolerance of ±1% at 25°C, its actual measurement error may increase significantly at other temperatures. Linear PTC Thermistors: Some silicon-based linear PTC thermistors maintain relatively stable resistance-temperature characteristics over a wide operating temperature range, helping achieve consistent measurements. However, their actual tolerance still depends on the specific device and its datasheet specifications. Temperature Sensitivity and Measurement Resolution Sensitivity describes how much a thermistor's resistance changes in response to a change in temperature. It reflects the sensor's ability to respond to temperature variations. Measurement resolution, on the other hand, refers to the smallest temperature change that the entire measurement system can detect. NTC Thermistors: The resistance-temperature relationship of an NTC thermistor is nonlinear, and its sensitivity varies with temperature. It generally has higher relative sensitivity at lower temperatures, while its relative sensitivity tends to decrease as temperature rises. Linear PTC Thermistors: Silicon-based linear PTC thermistors typically exhibit a more uniform resistance change with temperature, helping maintain a consistent measurement response across a relatively wide temperature range. It is important to note that the final measurement resolution depends not only on the thermistor itself but also on the ADC resolution, reference voltage, signal noise, and external circuit design. Linearization: Simplifying Circuit Design Ideally, a sensor's output signal should have a linear relationship with the measured temperature. This simplifies subsequent data processing and temperature conversion. Challenges with NTC Thermistors: The resistance-temperature (R-T) relationship of an NTC thermistor is strongly nonlinear. To improve measurement linearity over the operating temperature range, software compensation is commonly used. Alternatively, additional components, such as a parallel resistor, can be added to the circuit for hardware linearization. Both approaches introduce some additional design or computational complexity. Figure 5. Improving the linearity of an NTC measurement circuit by adding a parallel resistor Advantages of Linear PTC Thermistors: Silicon-based linear PTC thermistors have an inherently more linear R-T characteristic, which can reduce the need for nonlinear compensation and simplify temperature conversion. However, the actual linearity of the output voltage relative to temperature also depends on the excitation circuit design. Figure 6. Linear PTC thermistors do not require a parallel resistor Self-Heating and Long-Term Drift Self-Heating: When current flows through a thermistor, Joule heating occurs, causing the device's own temperature to rise above the surrounding ambient temperature. This can introduce errors into temperature measurements. The degree of self-heating depends on the excitation method and the device's thermal dissipation conditions. For example, under constant-current excitation, thermistor power dissipation is: P = I² × R For an NTC thermistor, resistance decreases as temperature rises, so its power dissipation also decreases under constant-current excitation. Under constant-voltage excitation, however, power dissipation is: P = V² / R In this case, a decrease in NTC resistance may cause power dissipation to increase. Therefore, the excitation current or voltage should be properly controlled to prevent self-heating from affecting measurement accuracy. Long-Term Drift: Long-term drift refers to changes in a thermistor's resistance-temperature characteristics after prolonged operation or exposure to environmental factors such as temperature and humidity. It is closely related to the material, manufacturing process, operating temperature, and application environment. When selecting a thermistor, check the long-term stability and aging test data provided in its datasheet. This is particularly important in applications with demanding reliability requirements, such as automotive electronics and industrial control systems. Calibration All temperature sensors may exhibit component-to-component variations and system-level errors. Therefore, calibration is often necessary in applications requiring high measurement accuracy. NTC Thermistors: Because of their nonlinear R-T characteristics and potentially varying resistance errors across different temperatures, two-point or multipoint calibration may be required in applications with a wide temperature range or strict accuracy requirements. Linear PTC Thermistors: Thanks to their relatively linear characteristics, some devices can achieve good measurement accuracy with single-point calibration. However, multipoint calibration may still be necessary when high accuracy is required across the entire operating temperature range. The appropriate calibration method should be determined based on the required accuracy, operating temperature range, and device datasheet. 4. Software Processing: Converting Voltage into Temperature After the MCU reads the ADC value corresponding to V_TEMP, an algorithm is needed to convert it into an actual temperature value. Two common methods are used. Lookup Table Method A lookup table is created in advance to establish the relationship between resistance or ADC values and temperature. The MCU searches the table using the measured value to obtain the corresponding temperature. Interpolation can also be used to improve conversion accuracy. This method offers fast execution and simple implementation, but it requires additional memory. It is a practical option for MCUs with limited computational resources. Equation-Based Calculation Mathematical models are used to fit the thermistor's R-T curve and convert the measured resistance into temperature. For NTC Thermistors: The Steinhart-Hart equation is commonly used: 1/T = A + B*ln(R) + C*[ln(R)]³ Where T is the absolute temperature in Kelvin (K), R is the thermistor resistance, and A, B, and C are coefficients determined by the device's characteristics. For Linear PTC Thermistors: If the device has a sufficiently linear resistance-temperature relationship, a simple linear equation can be used: T = T₀ + (R − R₀) / (α × R₀) Where T₀ is the reference temperature, R₀ is the resistance at that temperature, and α is the temperature coefficient. For applications requiring higher accuracy, polynomial fitting or lookup tables can also be used to compensate for deviations from ideal linearity. 5. PCB Layout Considerations for Thermistor Circuits Selecting the right thermistor and designing an appropriate measurement circuit are only part of the process. PCB layout also has a direct impact on temperature measurement accuracy. In precision temperature-sensing applications, sensor placement, signal routing, and grounding all require careful consideration. Proper Thermistor Placement The thermistor's position should be determined by the actual temperature measurement target. If the thermistor is used to monitor the temperature of a MOSFET, power resistor, or power management IC, it should be placed as close as practical to the target heat-generating component to minimize temperature differences caused by thermal conduction paths. If it is used for ambient temperature sensing, it should be kept away from power components, heatsinks, and other significant heat sources to prevent localized heating from affecting the readings. Avoid unnecessary large copper areas or other thermally conductive structures that may transfer heat from nearby components to the thermistor, unless these structures are intentionally part of the thermal sensing design. Optimize Analog Signal Routing The output of a thermistor measurement circuit is an analog signal, which can be affected by electromagnetic interference and noise from other circuits. Keep the signal path between the thermistor and the MCU ADC input as short as practical. Avoid routing the signal parallel to high-frequency clock lines, switching nodes, or high-current traces over long distances. If necessary, add an appropriate RC filter at the ADC input to suppress high-frequency noise. Consider Grounding and ADC Reference Voltage Grounding and reference voltage stability also affect temperature measurement accuracy. Avoid sharing long ground paths between the thermistor measurement circuit and high-current return paths to reduce errors caused by ground potential variations. Ensure that the ADC reference voltage is stable to prevent power supply noise from affecting conversion results. For voltage divider measurement circuits, consider using a ratiometric measurement approach in which the divider supply and ADC reference voltage are the same. This helps reduce errors caused by supply voltage fluctuations. 6. Summary and Thermistor Selection Guide NTC and linear PTC thermistors each have their own advantages. The appropriate choice depends on the measurement temperature range, accuracy requirements, cost, and circuit design complexity. Key Selection Considerations: If cost is a major concern and the measurement range is relatively narrow with moderate accuracy requirements, a traditional NTC thermistor is still an excellent choice. It offers low cost, mature technology, and a wide range of available components. However, its nonlinear characteristics and potential temperature compensation requirements should be taken into account. If an application requires better temperature linearity, stable performance across the operating temperature range, and simpler signal processing, a silicon-based linear PTC thermistor may be worth considering. Its relatively linear characteristics can simplify temperature conversion, but the actual measurement accuracy, operating range, and calibration requirements must still be evaluated based on the specific device specifications. In practical designs, thermistor measurement performance depends not only on the sensor itself but also on the excitation circuit, ADC configuration, sensor placement, and thermistor PCB layout. By considering component selection, circuit design, and PCB layout together, designers can develop more accurate and reliable temperature monitoring systems. NTC, PTC, and PCB Layout by: Mila Nov 18,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCB Design & Layout thermistor circuit NTC thermistor PTC thermistor NTC vs PTC thermistor thermistor pcb Temperature monitoring is essential for protecting electronic components, maintaining system stability, and ensuring reliable operation. Whether preventing a battery from overheating or keeping an industrial motor within its operating temperature range, accurate temperature sensing plays an important role. Among various temperature sensors, thermistors are widely used because of their simple structure, low cost, and fast response. This article explains how thermistors work, explores common measurement circuits, discusses key performance parameters, and compares NTC and PTC thermistors to help guide component selection and PCB design . 1. What Is a Thermistor? Understanding How It Works Working Principle: A thermistor is a resistor whose resistance changes significantly with temperature. The name comes from the combination of "thermal" and "resistor." Its key characteristic is that its resistance varies in response to changes in its own temperature. This property allows a thermistor to convert temperature, a physical quantity, into a change in electrical resistance, which can then be converted into a measurable voltage signal through an external circuit. Figure 1. Different types of thermistors Two Main Types: Based on how their resistance changes with temperature, thermistors are generally divided into two categories: NTC (Negative Temperature Coefficient) Thermistors: Their resistance decreases as temperature increases. NTC thermistors are among the most widely used temperature-sensing components due to their low cost and high sensitivity. Common applications include battery temperature monitoring, power management, and household appliance temperature control. PTC (Positive Temperature Coefficient) Thermistors: Their resistance increases as temperature rises. Depending on their materials and resistance characteristics, PTC thermistors can be further divided into two types: Nonlinear (Switching-Type) PTC Thermistors: Their resistance increases sharply near a specific temperature, known as the Curie temperature. They are commonly used for overcurrent protection, overtemperature protection, and resettable fuses. Linear PTC Thermistors: Typically made from silicon, these devices have a relatively stable positive temperature coefficient. Their resistance increases approximately linearly with temperature, making them suitable for temperature measurement applications. Simply put, an NTC thermistor behaves like a component that offers less resistance as it gets hotter. A linear PTC thermistor works in the opposite way: its resistance increases with temperature, generally in a more uniform and predictable manner. 2. How to Read a Thermistor: Two Common Measurement Circuits A thermistor does not generate an electrical signal on its own. It requires an external excitation source to convert its resistance changes into a measurable voltage signal. The following are two commonly used measurement circuits. Voltage Divider Circuit (Constant-Voltage Excitation) Figure 2. Thermistor in a voltage divider configuration This is one of the simplest and most cost-effective thermistor measurement methods. A thermistor is connected in series with a fixed reference resistor and supplied by a stable voltage source, such as VCC. By measuring the voltage across one of the resistors, the temperature information can be obtained. Working Principle: When the temperature changes, the thermistor's resistance changes accordingly. According to the voltage divider principle, the output voltage, V_TEMP, also changes. By measuring this voltage, the thermistor resistance can be calculated, and the corresponding temperature can then be determined. Advantages: The circuit is simple, requires few components, and has a low implementation cost, making it suitable for many conventional temperature-sensing applications. Considerations: Variations in the supply voltage VCC can affect V_TEMP and introduce measurement errors. To reduce this effect, a ratiometric measurement method can be used. For example, the same voltage source can serve as both the excitation voltage for the divider and the ADC reference voltage. This helps cancel out the effects of supply voltage fluctuations. Constant-Current Excitation Circuit Figure 3. Thermistor measurement using constant-current excitation Another approach is to use a precision constant-current source (I BIAS ) to supply a stable current to the thermistor. Working Principle: According to Ohm's law, V = I × R. Since the current flowing through the thermistor remains constant, the voltage across it, V_TEMP, is proportional to its resistance: V TEMP = I BIAS × R THERMISTOR When the temperature changes and the thermistor resistance varies, the output voltage changes accordingly. Advantages: Within the operating range of the current source, the output voltage is linearly proportional to the thermistor resistance. This makes resistance measurement and signal processing more straightforward, especially in applications requiring relatively high measurement accuracy. Considerations: The accuracy, temperature drift, and output voltage range of the current source all affect measurement results. In addition, excessive excitation current can cause thermistor self-heating. Therefore, the bias current must be selected carefully. The Next Step: Signal Processing The resulting analog voltage signal, V TEMP , is typically sent to an analog-to-digital converter (ADC) input on a microcontroller (MCU) for digital processing. Alternatively, it can be sent to a voltage comparator and compared with a preset threshold voltage to implement a basic overtemperature alarm. Figure 4. Overtemperature threshold detection using a thermistor and comparator 3. Key Parameters for Improving Thermistor Performance and Accuracy When selecting a thermistor, its nominal resistance is not the only parameter to consider. The following characteristics also play an important role in determining temperature measurement accuracy, stability, and overall circuit complexity. Resistance Tolerance Resistance tolerance refers to the allowable deviation between a thermistor's actual resistance and its nominal resistance at a specified temperature, typically 25°C. For example, a tolerance of ±1% means the actual resistance can vary within 1% of the specified nominal value at that temperature. NTC Thermistors: The resistance tolerance of an NTC thermistor depends not only on its nominal resistance at 25°C but also on the tolerance of its B-value and other material characteristics. Therefore, even if an NTC thermistor has a resistance tolerance of ±1% at 25°C, its actual measurement error may increase significantly at other temperatures. Linear PTC Thermistors: Some silicon-based linear PTC thermistors maintain relatively stable resistance-temperature characteristics over a wide operating temperature range, helping achieve consistent measurements. However, their actual tolerance still depends on the specific device and its datasheet specifications. Temperature Sensitivity and Measurement Resolution Sensitivity describes how much a thermistor's resistance changes in response to a change in temperature. It reflects the sensor's ability to respond to temperature variations. Measurement resolution, on the other hand, refers to the smallest temperature change that the entire measurement system can detect. NTC Thermistors: The resistance-temperature relationship of an NTC thermistor is nonlinear, and its sensitivity varies with temperature. It generally has higher relative sensitivity at lower temperatures, while its relative sensitivity tends to decrease as temperature rises. Linear PTC Thermistors: Silicon-based linear PTC thermistors typically exhibit a more uniform resistance change with temperature, helping maintain a consistent measurement response across a relatively wide temperature range. It is important to note that the final measurement resolution depends not only on the thermistor itself but also on the ADC resolution, reference voltage, signal noise, and external circuit design. Linearization: Simplifying Circuit Design Ideally, a sensor's output signal should have a linear relationship with the measured temperature. This simplifies subsequent data processing and temperature conversion. Challenges with NTC Thermistors: The resistance-temperature (R-T) relationship of an NTC thermistor is strongly nonlinear. To improve measurement linearity over the operating temperature range, software compensation is commonly used. Alternatively, additional components, such as a parallel resistor, can be added to the circuit for hardware linearization. Both approaches introduce some additional design or computational complexity. Figure 5. Improving the linearity of an NTC measurement circuit by adding a parallel resistor Advantages of Linear PTC Thermistors: Silicon-based linear PTC thermistors have an inherently more linear R-T characteristic, which can reduce the need for nonlinear compensation and simplify temperature conversion. However, the actual linearity of the output voltage relative to temperature also depends on the excitation circuit design. Figure 6. Linear PTC thermistors do not require a parallel resistor Self-Heating and Long-Term Drift Self-Heating: When current flows through a thermistor, Joule heating occurs, causing the device's own temperature to rise above the surrounding ambient temperature. This can introduce errors into temperature measurements. The degree of self-heating depends on the excitation method and the device's thermal dissipation conditions. For example, under constant-current excitation, thermistor power dissipation is: P = I² × R For an NTC thermistor, resistance decreases as temperature rises, so its power dissipation also decreases under constant-current excitation. Under constant-voltage excitation, however, power dissipation is: P = V² / R In this case, a decrease in NTC resistance may cause power dissipation to increase. Therefore, the excitation current or voltage should be properly controlled to prevent self-heating from affecting measurement accuracy. Long-Term Drift: Long-term drift refers to changes in a thermistor's resistance-temperature characteristics after prolonged operation or exposure to environmental factors such as temperature and humidity. It is closely related to the material, manufacturing process, operating temperature, and application environment. When selecting a thermistor, check the long-term stability and aging test data provided in its datasheet. This is particularly important in applications with demanding reliability requirements, such as automotive electronics and industrial control systems. Calibration All temperature sensors may exhibit component-to-component variations and system-level errors. Therefore, calibration is often necessary in applications requiring high measurement accuracy. NTC Thermistors: Because of their nonlinear R-T characteristics and potentially varying resistance errors across different temperatures, two-point or multipoint calibration may be required in applications with a wide temperature range or strict accuracy requirements. Linear PTC Thermistors: Thanks to their relatively linear characteristics, some devices can achieve good measurement accuracy with single-point calibration. However, multipoint calibration may still be necessary when high accuracy is required across the entire operating temperature range. The appropriate calibration method should be determined based on the required accuracy, operating temperature range, and device datasheet. 4. Software Processing: Converting Voltage into Temperature After the MCU reads the ADC value corresponding to V_TEMP, an algorithm is needed to convert it into an actual temperature value. Two common methods are used. Lookup Table Method A lookup table is created in advance to establish the relationship between resistance or ADC values and temperature. The MCU searches the table using the measured value to obtain the corresponding temperature. Interpolation can also be used to improve conversion accuracy. This method offers fast execution and simple implementation, but it requires additional memory. It is a practical option for MCUs with limited computational resources. Equation-Based Calculation Mathematical models are used to fit the thermistor's R-T curve and convert the measured resistance into temperature. For NTC Thermistors: The Steinhart-Hart equation is commonly used: 1/T = A + B*ln(R) + C*[ln(R)]³ Where T is the absolute temperature in Kelvin (K), R is the thermistor resistance, and A, B, and C are coefficients determined by the device's characteristics. For Linear PTC Thermistors: If the device has a sufficiently linear resistance-temperature relationship, a simple linear equation can be used: T = T₀ + (R − R₀) / (α × R₀) Where T₀ is the reference temperature, R₀ is the resistance at that temperature, and α is the temperature coefficient. For applications requiring higher accuracy, polynomial fitting or lookup tables can also be used to compensate for deviations from ideal linearity. 5. PCB Layout Considerations for Thermistor Circuits Selecting the right thermistor and designing an appropriate measurement circuit are only part of the process. PCB layout also has a direct impact on temperature measurement accuracy. In precision temperature-sensing applications, sensor placement, signal routing, and grounding all require careful consideration. Proper Thermistor Placement The thermistor's position should be determined by the actual temperature measurement target. If the thermistor is used to monitor the temperature of a MOSFET, power resistor, or power management IC, it should be placed as close as practical to the target heat-generating component to minimize temperature differences caused by thermal conduction paths. If it is used for ambient temperature sensing, it should be kept away from power components, heatsinks, and other significant heat sources to prevent localized heating from affecting the readings. Avoid unnecessary large copper areas or other thermally conductive structures that may transfer heat from nearby components to the thermistor, unless these structures are intentionally part of the thermal sensing design. Optimize Analog Signal Routing The output of a thermistor measurement circuit is an analog signal, which can be affected by electromagnetic interference and noise from other circuits. Keep the signal path between the thermistor and the MCU ADC input as short as practical. Avoid routing the signal parallel to high-frequency clock lines, switching nodes, or high-current traces over long distances. If necessary, add an appropriate RC filter at the ADC input to suppress high-frequency noise. Consider Grounding and ADC Reference Voltage Grounding and reference voltage stability also affect temperature measurement accuracy. Avoid sharing long ground paths between the thermistor measurement circuit and high-current return paths to reduce errors caused by ground potential variations. Ensure that the ADC reference voltage is stable to prevent power supply noise from affecting conversion results. For voltage divider measurement circuits, consider using a ratiometric measurement approach in which the divider supply and ADC reference voltage are the same. This helps reduce errors caused by supply voltage fluctuations. 6. Summary and Thermistor Selection Guide NTC and linear PTC thermistors each have their own advantages. The appropriate choice depends on the measurement temperature range, accuracy requirements, cost, and circuit design complexity. Key Selection Considerations: If cost is a major concern and the measurement range is relatively narrow with moderate accuracy requirements, a traditional NTC thermistor is still an excellent choice. It offers low cost, mature technology, and a wide range of available components. However, its nonlinear characteristics and potential temperature compensation requirements should be taken into account. If an application requires better temperature linearity, stable performance across the operating temperature range, and simpler signal processing, a silicon-based linear PTC thermistor may be worth considering. Its relatively linear characteristics can simplify temperature conversion, but the actual measurement accuracy, operating range, and calibration requirements must still be evaluated based on the specific device specifications. In practical designs, thermistor measurement performance depends not only on the sensor itself but also on the excitation circuit, ADC configuration, sensor placement, and thermistor PCB layout. By considering component selection, circuit design, and PCB layout together, designers can develop more accurate and reliable temperature monitoring systems. NTC, PTC, and PCB Layout What Is the Purpose of a 1MΩ Resistor in a Crystal Oscillator Circuit PCBWay Store NewArrival Product - M5Stack Dial v1.1 Talking about the Composition of PCB Price Over the years, PCB price changes have been familiar with people inside and outside the industry, even though some people with years of experience in the PCB industry may not fully understand the ins and outs of this, so to analyze the main factors affecting pcb price: The diversity of prices caused by the different materials used in PCBs is based on common double-sided boards. Sheets generally include fr-4, cem-3, etc., and board thickness varies from 0.2mm to 5.0mm, and copper thickness varies from 0.5oz to 3oz. All of these have resulted in huge price differences on the sheet material; in solder mask inks, there are also certain price differences between ordinary thermoset oils and photosensitive green oils, and thus the diversity of materials has caused price diversity. The different production processes used by PCBs result in different production processes with different prices that will result in different costs. Such as gold-plated plates and sprayed tin plates, the production of the shape of the milling (milling) plate and beer (red) plate, the use of silk screen lines and dry film lines will have different costs, resulting in a variety of prices. The diversity of prices caused by the difficulty of the PCB itself Even if the material is the same, the process is the same, but the difficulty of the PCB itself will result in different costs. For example, if there are 1000 holes on both boards, the hole diameter of one board is more than 0.6mm and the hole diameter of the other board is less than 0.6mm, different drilling costs will be formed; if the two boards are the same, the linewidth is different. Differently, one type is larger than 0.2mm and one type is smaller than 0.2mm, which also causes different production costs, because the scrap rate of difficult plates is high, the inevitable cost is increased, and the price diversity is thus caused. Different customer requirements will also cause different prices The level of customer demand will directly affect the plate production rate, such as a board by ipc-a-600e, class1 requirements have a 98% pass rate, but according to class3 requirements may be only 90% The passing rate, resulting in different costs for the mill, eventually led to a change in the price of the product. The diversity of prices caused by different PCB manufacturers even if the same product, but because of different manufacturers of technology and equipment, different levels of technology, will also form a different cost, nowadays many manufacturers like to produce tin spray plate, because the process is simple, low cost, but Some manufacturers also produce gold-plated plates, resulting in higher scrap rates and higher costs. Therefore, they prefer to produce tin-spray plates, so their prices for tin-spray plates are lower than those for gold-plated plates. The price difference caused by different payment methods At present, PCB manufacturers generally adjust PCB prices according to different payment methods, ranging from 5% to 10%, which also results in price differences. Diversification of prices caused by regional differences At present, from the geographical point of view, prices have been increasing from south to north. There are certain differences in prices in different regions, and thus different regions have also caused price diversity. Engineer 01.PPE - Pre Production Engineering Customer supplied data (gerber) is used to produce the manufacturing data for the specific PCB (artworks for imaging processes and drill data for drilling programs). Engineers compare demands/specifications against capabilities to ensure compliance and also determine the process steps and associated checks. No changes are allowed without PCBWay Group permission. 02.Board Cutting (Copper Clad Laminate Cutting) PCB production starts with a large piece of sheet material. Due to the limitations of PCB production equipment and manufacture capabilities, the factory has requirements for its minimum and maximum processing size. Therefore, under the guidance of manufacture instruction (MI), the raw material of PCB (Copper Clad Laminate ) needs to be cut into the processing size by automatic cutting machine before production. 03.Print inner layers Stage 1 is to transfer the image using an artwork film to the board surface, using photosensitive dry-film and UV light, which will polymerise the dry film exposed by the artwork. This step of the process is performed in a clean room.
Imaging – The process of transferring electronic data to the photo-plotter, which in turn uses light to transfer a negative image circuitry pattern onto the panel or film. 04.Etch inner layers Stage 2 is to remove the unwanted copper from the panel using etching. Once this copper has been removed, the remaining dry film is then removed leaving behind the copper circuitry that matches the design.
Etching – The chemical, or chemical and electrolytic, removal of unwanted portions of conductive or resistive material. 05.Inner layer Automatic Optical Inspection(AOI) Inspection of the circuitry against digital “images” to verify that the circuitry matches the design and that it is free from defects. Achieved through scanning of the board and then trained inspectors will verify any anomalies that the scanning process has highlighted. PCBWay Group allows no repair of open circuits. 06.Lay-up and bond (Lamination) The inner layers have an oxide layer applied and then “stacked” together with pre-preg providing insulation between layers and copper foil is added to the top and bottom of the stack. The lamination process consists of placing the internal layers under extreme temperature (375 degrees Fahrenheit) and pressure (275 to 400 psi) while laminating with a photosensitive dry resist. The PCB is allowed to cure at a high temperature, the pressure is slowly released and then the material is slowly cooled. 07.Drilling the PCB We now have to drill the holes that will subsequently create electrical connections within the multilayer PCB. This is a mechanical drilling process that must be optimised so that we can achieve registration to all of the the inner layer connections. The panels can be stacked at this process. The drilling can also be done by a laser drill 08.Electroless copper deposition The first step in the plating process is the chemical deposition of a very thin layer of copper on the hole walls. PTH provides a very thin deposit of copper that covers the hole wall and the complete panel. A complex chemical process that must be strictly controlled to allow a reliable deposit of copper to be plated even onto the non-metallic hole wall. Whilst not a sufficient amount of copper on its own, we now have electrical continuity between layers and through the holes.Panel plating follows on from PTH to provide a thicker deposit of copper on top of the PTH deposit – typically 5 to 8 um. The combination is used to optimise the amount of copper that is to be plated and etched in order to achieve the track and gap demands. 09.Image the outer layers Similar to the inner layer process (image transfer using photosensitive dry film, exposure to UV light and etching), but with one main difference – we will remove the dry film where we want to keep the copper/define circuitry – so we can plate additional copper later in the process. This step of the process is performed in a clean room. 10.Plating Second electrolytic plating stage, where the additional plating is deposited in areas without dry film (circuitry). Once the copper has been plated, tin is applied to protect the plated copper. 11.Etch outer layer This is normally a three step process. The first step is to remove the blue dry film. The second step is to etch away the exposed/unwanted copper whilst the tin deposit acts an etch resist protecting the copper we need. The third and final step is to chemically remove the tin deposit leaving the circuitry. 12.Outer layer AOI Just like with inner layer AOI the imaged and etched panel is scanned to make sure that the circuitry meets design and that it is free from defects. Again no repair of open circuits are allowed under PCBWay demands. 13.Soldermask Soldermask ink is applied over the whole PCB surface. Using artworks and UV light we expose certain areas to the UV and those areas not exposed are removed during the chemical development process – typically the areas which are to be used as solderable surfaces. The remaining soldermask is then fully cured making it a resilient finish.
This step of the process is performed in a clean room. 14.Surface finish Various finishes are then applied to the exposed copper areas. This is to enable protection of the surface and good solderability. The various finishes can include Electroless Nickel Immersion Gold, HASL, Immersion Silver etc. Thicknesses and solderability tests are always carried out. 15.Profile This is the process of cutting the manufac-turing panels into specific sizes and shapes based upon the customer design as defined within the gerber data. There are 3 main options available when providing the array or selling panel – scoring, routing or punching. All dimensions are measured against the customer supplied drawing to ensure the panel is dimensionally correct. 16.Electrical test Used for checking the integrity of the tracks and the through hole interconnections – checking to ensure there are no open circuits or no short circuits on the finished board. There are three test methods, flying probe for smaller volumes,fixture based for volumes and 4-wire Kelvin testing (For PCBs use in automotive, or aerospace applications).We electrically test every PCB against the original board data. Using a flying probe tester we check each net to ensure that it is complete (no open circuits) and does not short to any other net. 17.Final inspection In the last step of the process a team of sharp-eyed inspectors give each PCB a final careful check-over.Visual checking the PCB against acceptance criteria and using PCBWay “approved” inspectors. Using manual visual inspection and AVI – compares PCB to gerber and has a faster checking speed that human eyes, but still requires human verification. All orders are also subjected to a full inspection including dimensional, solderability, etc. 18.Packaging Boards are wrapped using materials that comply with the PCBWay Packaging demands (ESD etcetera) and then boxed prior to be being shipped using the requested mode of transport. Engineer 01.PPE - Pre Production Engineering Customer supplied data (gerber) is used to produce the manufacturing data for the specific PCB (artworks for imaging processes and drill data for drilling programs). Engineers compare demands/specifications against capabilities to ensure compliance and also determine the process steps and associated checks. No changes are allowed without PCBWay Group permission. 02.Board Cutting (Copper Clad Laminate Cutting) PCB production starts with a large piece of sheet material. Due to the limitations of PCB production equipment and manufacture capabilities, the factory has requirements for its minimum and maximum processing size. Therefore, under the guidance of manufacture instruction (MI), the raw material of PCB (Copper Clad Laminate ) needs to be cut into the processing size by automatic cutting machine before production. 03.Print inner layers Stage 1 is to transfer the image using an artwork film to the board surface, using photosensitive dry-film and UV light, which will polymerise the dry film exposed by the artwork. This step of the process is performed in a clean room.
Imaging – The process of transferring electronic data to the photo-plotter, which in turn uses light to transfer a negative image circuitry pattern onto the panel or film. 04.Etch inner layers Stage 2 is to remove the unwanted copper from the panel using etching. Once this copper has been removed, the remaining dry film is then removed leaving behind the copper circuitry that matches the design.
Etching – The chemical, or chemical and electrolytic, removal of unwanted portions of conductive or resistive material. 05.Inner layer Automatic Optical Inspection(AOI) Inspection of the circuitry against digital “images” to verify that the circuitry matches the design and that it is free from defects. Achieved through scanning of the board and then trained inspectors will verify any anomalies that the scanning process has highlighted. PCBWay Group allows no repair of open circuits. 06.Lay-up and bond (Lamination) The inner layers have an oxide layer applied and then “stacked” together with pre-preg providing insulation between layers and copper foil is added to the top and bottom of the stack. The lamination process consists of placing the internal layers under extreme temperature (375 degrees Fahrenheit) and pressure (275 to 400 psi) while laminating with a photosensitive dry resist. The PCB is allowed to cure at a high temperature, the pressure is slowly released and then the material is slowly cooled. 07.Drilling the PCB We now have to drill the holes that will subsequently create electrical connections within the multilayer PCB. This is a mechanical drilling process that must be optimised so that we can achieve registration to all of the the inner layer connections. The panels can be stacked at this process. The drilling can also be done by a laser drill 08.Electroless copper deposition The first step in the plating process is the chemical deposition of a very thin layer of copper on the hole walls. PTH provides a very thin deposit of copper that covers the hole wall and the complete panel. A complex chemical process that must be strictly controlled to allow a reliable deposit of copper to be plated even onto the non-metallic hole wall. Whilst not a sufficient amount of copper on its own, we now have electrical continuity between layers and through the holes.Panel plating follows on from PTH to provide a thicker deposit of copper on top of the PTH deposit – typically 5 to 8 um. The combination is used to optimise the amount of copper that is to be plated and etched in order to achieve the track and gap demands. 09.Image the outer layers Similar to the inner layer process (image transfer using photosensitive dry film, exposure to UV light and etching), but with one main difference – we will remove the dry film where we want to keep the copper/define circuitry – so we can plate additional copper later in the process. This step of the process is performed in a clean room. 10.Plating Second electrolytic plating stage, where the additional plating is deposited in areas without dry film (circuitry). Once the copper has been plated, tin is applied to protect the plated copper. 11.Etch outer layer This is normally a three step process. The first step is to remove the blue dry film. The second step is to etch away the exposed/unwanted copper whilst the tin deposit acts an etch resist protecting the copper we need. The third and final step is to chemically remove the tin deposit leaving the circuitry. 12.Outer layer AOI Just like with inner layer AOI the imaged and etched panel is scanned to make sure that the circuitry meets design and that it is free from defects. Again no repair of open circuits are allowed under PCBWay demands. 13.Soldermask Soldermask ink is applied over the whole PCB surface. Using artworks and UV light we expose certain areas to the UV and those areas not exposed are removed during the chemical development process – typically the areas which are to be used as solderable surfaces. The remaining soldermask is then fully cured making it a resilient finish.
This step of the process is performed in a clean room. 14.Surface finish Various finishes are then applied to the exposed copper areas. This is to enable protection of the surface and good solderability. The various finishes can include Electroless Nickel Immersion Gold, HASL, Immersion Silver etc. Thicknesses and solderability tests are always carried out. 15.Profile This is the process of cutting the manufac-turing panels into specific sizes and shapes based upon the customer design as defined within the gerber data. There are 3 main options available when providing the array or selling panel – scoring, routing or punching. All dimensions are measured against the customer supplied drawing to ensure the panel is dimensionally correct. 16.Electrical test Used for checking the integrity of the tracks and the through hole interconnections – checking to ensure there are no open circuits or no short circuits on the finished board. There are three test methods, flying probe for smaller volumes,fixture based for volumes and 4-wire Kelvin testing (For PCBs use in automotive, or aerospace applications).We electrically test every PCB against the original board data. Using a flying probe tester we check each net to ensure that it is complete (no open circuits) and does not short to any other net. 17.Final inspection In the last step of the process a team of sharp-eyed inspectors give each PCB a final careful check-over.Visual checking the PCB against acceptance criteria and using PCBWay “approved” inspectors. Using manual visual inspection and AVI – compares PCB to gerber and has a faster checking speed that human eyes, but still requires human verification. All orders are also subjected to a full inspection including dimensional, solderability, etc. 18.Packaging Boards are wrapped using materials that comply with the PCBWay Packaging demands (ESD etcetera) and then boxed prior to be being shipped using the requested mode of transport. NTC, PTC, and PCB Layout What Is the Purpose of a 1MΩ Resistor in a Crystal Oscillator Circuit PCBWay Store NewArrival Product - M5Stack Dial v1.1 BGA Assembly Capabilities When it comes to BGA assembly, let's first understand what BGA is. BGAs (Ball Grid Arrays) are a type of IC package where the pins are placed in the form of solder balls. Compared to traditional packaging technologies such as DIP (Dual In-line Package) or QFP (Quad Flat Package), BGA employs a higher-density pin layout. With technological advancements, there is an increasing demand in PCB design for complex and small-sized chips. These chips enable higher integration and functionality within smaller spaces. Hence, there is a need for a packaging method that can accommodate these chips with higher I/O density while maintaining cost-effectiveness. BGA (Ball Grid Array) is precisely such a packaging method that meets these requirements. What is BGA Assembly? BGA assembly refers to the process of mounting a Ball Grid Array (BGA) onto a PCB using the reflow soldering technique. BGA is a surface-mounted component that utilizes an array of solder balls for electrical interconnection. As the circuit board passes through a solder reflow oven, these solder balls melt, forming electrical connections. Steps of BGA Assembly The BGA assembly process typically involves the following steps: PCB Preparation: The PCB is prepared by applying solder paste to the pads where the BGA will be mounted. The solder paste is a mixture of solder alloy particles and flux, which helps with the soldering process. Placement of BGAs: The BGAs, which consist of the integrated circuit chip with solder balls on the bottom, are placed onto the prepared PCB. This is typically done using automated pick-and-place machines or other assembly equipment. Reflow Soldering: The assembled PCB with the placed BGAs is then passed through a reflow oven. The reflow oven heats the PCB to a specific temperature that melts the solder paste, causing the solder balls of the BGAs to reflow and establish electrical connections with the PCB pads. Cooling and Inspection: After the solder reflow process, the PCB is cooled down to solidify the solder joints. It is then inspected for any defects, such as misalignment, shorts, or open connections. Automated optical inspection (AOI) or X-ray inspection may be used for this purpose. Secondary Processes: Depending on the specific requirements, additional processes such as cleaning, testing, and conformal coating may be performed after BGA assembly to ensure the reliability and quality of the finished product. Advantages of BGA Assembly Small footprint BGA packaging consists of the chip, interconnects, a thin substrate, and an encapsulation cover. There are few exposed components and the package has a minimal number of pins. The overall height of the chip on the PCB can be as low as 1.2 millimeters. Robustness BGA packaging is highly robust. Unlike QFP with a 20mil pitch, BGA does not have pins that can bend or break. Generally, BGA removal requires the use of a BGA rework station at high temperatures. Lower parasitic inductance and capacitance With short pins and low assembly height, BGA packaging exhibits low parasitic inductance and capacitance, resulting in excellent electrical performance. Increased storage space Compared to other packaging types, BGA packaging has only one-third of the volume and approximately 1.2 times the chip area. Memory and operational products using BGA packaging can achieve more than a 2.1-fold increase in storage capacity and operational speed. High stability Due to the direct extension of pins from the center of the chip in BGA packaging, the transmission paths for various signals are effectively shortened, reducing signal attenuation and improving response speed and anti-interference capabilities. This enhances the stability of the product. Good heat dissipation BGA offers excellent heat dissipation performance, with the chip temperature approaching the ambient temperature during operation. Convenient for rework The pins of BGA packaging are neatly arranged on the bottom, making it easy to locate damaged areas for removal. This facilitates the rework of BGA chips. Avoidance of wiring chaos BGA packaging allows for placing many power and ground pins in the center, with I/O pins positioned on the periphery. Pre-routing can be done on the BGA substrate, avoiding chaotic wiring of I/O pins. PCBWay BGA Assembly Capabilities PCBWay is a globally renowned manufacturer for PCB fabrication and PCB assembly. BGA assembly service is one of the many service types we offer. PCBWay can provide you with high-quality and cost-effective BGA assembly for your PCBs. The minimum pitch for BGA assembly that we can accommodate is 0.25mm 0.3mm .
